title: Real numbers
competency: Define real numbers, compare them, and find real numbers between any two real numbers.

keywords.def: Any rational or irrational number. Every point on the number line is a real number. The set is written ℝ.
A number that can be written a/b with integers a, b and b ≠ 0. The set is written ℚ.
A decimal that neither ends nor repeats, such as √2 or π. It cannot be written as a/b.
For real a and b, exactly one of a < b, a = b, a > b is true.
If a < b and b < c, then a < c.

en.text: A real number is either rational or irrational. Together they make the set ℝ. Every decimal is exactly one point on the number line. Every point on the line is exactly one decimal.

screens.title: Two lists, one set?
screens.text: Abebe lists 3/4, −2 and 0.5. Almaz lists √2 and π. Activity 1.14 asks about such lists.
screens.ask: Is there one set that holds both lists?
opts: Yes, one set holds them all
Only Abebe's list is a set

screens.title: Real numbers
paras: Activity 1.14 asks: how are points on the number line and decimals related?
Every decimal, rational or irrational, is exactly one point on the number line. Every point is exactly one decimal.
Definition 1.7: A number is a real number if it is either rational or irrational.
The set of real numbers, ℝ, is the union of the rational and the irrational numbers: ℝ = {x : x is rational or x is irrational}.
screens.note: The real numbers are made of two non-overlapping parts: rational and irrational.

screens.title: Real numbers
defs: A number that is either rational or irrational. The set of all real numbers is written ℝ.

screens.title: Which is true?
screens.text: Think about how ℝ is built.
opts: Some numbers are both rational and irrational
π is not a real number
screens.why: ℝ is the union of the rationals and the irrationals.
screens.clue: The two parts of ℝ do not overlap, and together they fill it.

screens.title: Rational or irrational?
screens.text: Every one of these is a real number. Sort them into the two parts of ℝ.
items: It is a fraction of two integers.
Its decimal neither ends nor repeats.
screens.why: Rational decimals end or repeat. Irrational decimals do neither.
screens.clue: Ask: does the decimal end or repeat?

screens.title: Fill in the set
screens.ask: ℝ is the union of the rational numbers and the ___ numbers.
screens.why: Definition 1.7: a real number is rational or irrational.
screens.clue: Which kind of number is not rational?

screens.title: A plot in Bahir Dar
screens.text: Hana has a square plot in Bahir Dar with area 2 m². Its side is √2 m. The side length is a real number.
screens.why: √2 is irrational, and every irrational number is real.
screens.clue: Is √2 rational or irrational? Both kinds belong to ℝ.
screens.worked: √2 = 1.41421… never ends or repeats, so it is irrational. Irrational numbers are real. So the side is a real number.

en.text: Each real number is one point on the number line, so any two can be compared. Exactly one of a < b, a = b, a > b is true. For non-negative numbers, compare the squares. Between any two real numbers there are infinitely many more.

screens.ask: Which number is bigger? Take a guess.
screens.after: The book compares them by squaring. Read on.

screens.title: Comparing real numbers
paras: Each real number is one point on the number line. So any two real numbers can be compared.
Trichotomy: for real a and b, exactly one of a < b, a = b, a > b is true.
Transitive: if a < b and b < c, then a < c.
For non-negative a and b: if a² < b², then a < b.

screens.title: Two rules of order
defs: For real a and b, exactly one of a < b, a = b, a > b is true.
If a < b and b < c, then a < c.

screens.title: Use the transitive rule
screens.text: You know that a < b and b < c.
screens.why: The transitive property: a is left of b, and b is left of c.
screens.clue: Place a, b and c on a number line.

screens.text: Four ways to compare real numbers.
steps: (a) −8 is left of −2 on the number line, so −8 < −2.

screens.title: Compare by squaring
screens.worked: (3√2)² = 9 × 2 = 18. (2√3)² = 4 × 3 = 12. Both numbers are positive and 18 > 12, so 3√2 > 2√3.

screens.title: Real numbers between two numbers
paras: Is there a real number between 2 and 4.2? Take the average: (2 + 4.2)/2 = 3.1, and 2 < 3.1 < 4.2.
Averaging again gives 2.55, between 2 and 3.1. It also gives 3.65, between 3.1 and 4.2.
We can keep doing this for ever. So there are infinitely many real numbers between any two real numbers.

screens.title: Find one in between
screens.clue: Take the average of the two numbers.

screens.title: Teff prices in Adama
screens.text: One shop in Adama sells a kilo of teff for 95 birr. Another sells it for 101 birr. A third shop charges the average of the two.
screens.clue: Add the two prices, then divide by 2.

items.why: The hundredths digit 3 is less than 5.
items.clue: Compare digit by digit from the left.
For negatives, the one closer to 0 is bigger.
Write both as decimals to 4 places.

Its decimal ends, like 0.75, or repeats, like 0.333…
An irrational decimal neither ends nor repeats.
